voice.voice_0922f78e1ce26ca8: What are most clouds made of?
voice.voice_90b81693967ff28e: What does water become when it freezes?
voice.voice_ff5edd5a1919fcb7: What helps a green plant make its food?
voice.voice_7f15ff2a4bc7cc16: What carries most sounds from across a room to your ears?
voice.voice_2a2eb85027e142d9: What do we call a sound that bounces back to us?
voice.voice_b5392f62113b434d: What pumps blood around your body?

voice.voice_bca5aed2e60a0812: What can a caterpillar grow into?

voice.voice_808957d772415aff: Sunlight has many colors, like a rainbow. Tiny bits of air scatter blue light in all directions, so the sky looks blue.
voice.voice_53baacb915c1e217: Grass has a green helper called chlorophyll that catches sunlight. Think of each blade as a little solar panel that helps the grass make food.
voice.voice_6133ce60d83b5d12: Sleep gives your body time to rest and your brain time to sort what you learned. It is a bit like putting your toys back in their boxes after playing.
voice.voice_bddcaf12b22da1c2: Rivers carry tiny bits of salt from rocks into the sea. When water rises into the air, the salt stays behind, a little like salt left in a bowl after water dries.
voice.voice_27207c6baeb48f36: Clouds are full of tiny drops of water that bump together and grow. When they get heavy enough, they fall like drops from a wet sponge.
voice.voice_4088884c4b8ab522: Stars are huge balls of hot gas that make their own light. They look like tiny lights because most are very far away. The Sun is our closest star.
voice.voice_e302bb35175e9a7e: The Moon shines because sunlight bounces off its surface. Think of it like a ball lit by a flashlight.
voice.voice_04c0580bd0257a02: Earth spins like a top. When your part faces the Sun it is day, and when it turns away it is night.
voice.voice_02e6c2e9649e2ca1: Plants use sunlight, air, and water to make food and grow. Their roots take in water like little drinking straws.
voice.voice_e3cf049fecf4ced9: Clouds are made of tiny drops of water or bits of ice. A cloud is a little like fog floating high above the ground.
voice.voice_fab2fa6148a46799: When water gets cold enough, its tiny pieces slow down and lock together to make ice. Think of loose building blocks snapping into a solid shape.
voice.voice_3ac791f6ff38b949: When sunlight passes through raindrops, the drops spread its colors out. Each drop is a bit like a tiny piece of shiny glass.
voice.voice_2dd20db2b8c3342f: Dogs let heat out when they pant. Moving air over their wet tongues cools them a little, like a breeze on damp skin.
voice.voice_7402736cebec4e21: A cat makes a purr by moving parts in its throat as it breathes. Cats often purr when relaxed, a little like a quiet motor.
voice.voice_23429839ff570f19: Birds push air down with their wings, and the air pushes the birds up. You can think of their wings as paddles that push against the air.
voice.voice_6d07049b42af90bf: Fish pass water over their gills, which pick up oxygen from the water. Gills do a job a little like your lungs, but in water.
voice.voice_7a793a257220d30c: Bees can make a buzz by moving their wings very fast. The quick movements shake the air, like a tiny drum beating very quickly.
voice.voice_7d35bf26effc9e4c: A caterpillar changes inside a shell called a chrysalis. When that change is done, a butterfly comes out with wings.
voice.voice_95794c733c11ffd6: Your heart squeezes to push blood through your body. It works like a little pump that keeps moving while you work, play, or sleep.
voice.voice_121324832ffdd0ad: Your bones hold your body up and protect parts inside you. Together, they make a frame a bit like the beams that hold up a house.
voice.voice_9c53f856ba78fe7c: Sound makes the air wiggle, and those wiggles move a thin part inside your ear. Your ear and brain work together to tell you what made the sound.
voice.voice_c8ba5d4c516266d8: An echo happens when sound bounces off something and comes back to you. It is like rolling a ball toward a wall and watching it bounce back.
voice.voice_f9d5aeff22fdd6fc: A sneeze is a quick blast of air that can clear dust from your nose. It is like your nose’s own little cleaning puff.
voice.voice_4afb9b98befdf54d: Lightning heats the air around it very quickly. That air pushes outward, making the loud sound we call thunder.
voice.voice_a37e3a3ef3ea89f3: Snow starts as tiny bits of ice inside clouds. More ice sticks to them as they grow, like little building blocks making a pattern.
voice.voice_4d781a43e9e5f432: Sunlight warms some places more than others. Air moves as warmer air rises, and that moving air is wind.
voice.voice_ee1f7d3a6cf94d7a: Water in a puddle can turn into a gas and mix with the air. That is why a puddle grows smaller like wet clothes drying on a line.
voice.voice_99cdf34649336893: A candle flame gets its fuel from melted wax that moves up the wick. The wick is like a tiny straw that brings wax to the flame.
voice.voice_2ee93125261759fd: Saturn’s rings are made of many pieces of ice and rock moving around the planet. From far away, those pieces look like wide, bright bands.
voice.voice_ca3bb7992b6430cb: Gravity pulls things toward Earth. It is like an invisible tug that keeps your feet on the ground and brings a dropped ball back down.
voice.voice_be36cd625e17d1bf: The hero wears a round green mask with two very big goggles.
voice.voice_161a4db5538a4c25: Under the goggles there is a wide, happy smile.
voice.voice_2af0ab794fd44d01: The suit is green, with a bright yellow stripe across the chest.
voice.voice_4069dffd3619dd02: Each hand has four fingers, and every fingertip is a big round sticky dot.
voice.voice_d281e4a7c749d8c6: A short yellow cape flutters behind the hero.
voice.voice_e8e7eb266acae122: A long curly tail swings from the back, with a little star at the tip.
voice.voice_3557ae99fa02f821: Child. Children come in many heights, so this explorer is just one example.
voice.voice_b4a5d9db707f5978: Blue whale. The biggest animal on Earth eats tiny creatures called krill.
voice.voice_173a684de2800e20: Mount Everest. Everest's snowy peak is the highest spot above sea level on Earth.
voice.voice_1e43c451c563e308: Moon. The Moon looks bright because it reflects light from the Sun.
voice.voice_4f71cb60f6c4b9a9: Earth. Oceans cover most of Earth, giving our home its blue color from space.
voice.voice_2cae80848e5f1442: Jupiter. Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a giant storm.
voice.voice_03f89d431000c501: Sun. Sunlight takes about eight minutes to reach Earth.
voice.voice_c1b66badb14ab9c0: Betelgeuse. This reddish star is part of a group of stars we call Orion.
voice.voice_279630fa56e0bedf: Let us clap our hands together! Clap, clap, clap!
voice.voice_c65d2f21fcf5bbd3: Peek-a-boo! I see you! Wave your hand!
voice.voice_16c07eb389f160ee: Look, a friendly cow! What does the cow say? Moooo!
voice.voice_c43d4f87ef50db6b: Look, a cow! The cow says moo, moo!
voice.voice_4a9be67925584e43: Look, a cat! The cat says meow, meow!
voice.voice_f4deea3cf7343321: Look, a dog! The dog says woof, woof!
voice.voice_7872f40816d7c8ce: Let's ask a grown-up! We can explore animals or space together.
voice.voice_9aecca2e184ab778: Great question! Let's ask a grown-up and find out together.
voice.voice_b5814a340c66d554: I didn't hear that, try again!
voice.voice_2533155913101cf6: Let's take a little break and try again soon!
